Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer reports recurrent frontal headaches, intermittent palpitations, shortness of breath at rest, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite with 5 lb unintentional weight loss, and decreased libido since changing jobs; high work stress (7–8/10).
- Plan is in-person review for examination of heart and lungs and blood tests related to thyroxine; patient to book via app. No medications initiated today.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Recurrent headaches since job change; occur mostly at work (meetings, on laptop), frontal location, intermittent, severe enough to affect work.
- Associated symptoms: slight nausea; reduced appetite.
- Pertinent negatives/positives: No prior history of similar headaches before this period; not typically on commute; not clearly triggered by exercise.
- Social/occupational context: Lawyer in London; job is high stress (7–8/10) with significant reading/computer time.

Issue 2:
- Intermittent palpitations and episodes of feeling short of breath at rest (e.g., at desk; sometimes noted in elevator); approximately once daily or more.
- Pertinent negatives/positives: No shortness of breath with exercise; episodes occur at different times, not all simultaneously.
- Associated symptom: Bilateral hand tingling; no leg tingling.

Issue 3:
- Unintentional weight loss and decreased libido.
- Details: 5 lb weight loss, unintentional; reduced appetite. Clothes not noticeably looser; no external comments on weight loss.
- Timeline: Since job change.

Medications:
- Thyroxine — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Thyroid disease: patient reports “hyperthyroidism,” but is taking thyroxine (typically for hypothyroidism) — conflict noted.
- No other medical conditions reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer (London); work involves meetings and computer use.
- Alcohol: ~2 glasses of wine once weekly.
- Smoking: Denies.
- Recreational drugs: Denies.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed during this consult (telehealth).
- No vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person appointment for physical examination (heart and respiratory assessment).
- Order blood tests related to thyroxine use (specific tests not documented).
- Defer starting any new medications until after in-person assessment.
- Patient to book appointment via the clinic app; clinician to brief colleague on today’s history.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergy status confirmation; medication dosing/route/frequency; vitals; detailed neurological exam; headache red flags (vision changes, photophobia, focal deficits), mood/anxiety screening; full ROS; family history; preventive care history; vaccination status.
- Internal conflicts: Patient states “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine (commonly for hypothyroidism) — conflict noted. Initial booking note mentioned “feeling hot,” patient clarified symptoms as shortness of breath — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Some pauses/inaudible or unclear fragments; overall history obtainable but certain details were incomplete.
